data.narrative: The student turned a risk-ordered plan into a coherent stack of vertical slices with clear in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries. The strongest moment was their response to stakeholder pressure: they preserved the thin booking slice, added a separate payment spike, and made the tradeoff cost explicit instead of quietly inflating scope.

dimension_scores.observation: The slice set reflects a strong grasp of the marketplace requirements and a deliberate understanding of what had to be deferred in each increment.
dimension_scores.evidence: They defined slices with explicit anti-scope such as excluding "auth, payments, email, search, provider self-service, cancellations, reviews, and real-time availability" from Slice 1.

dimension_scores.observation: The slices build on each other in a logical order, with each later slice consuming a stable contract or capability established earlier.
dimension_scores.evidence: They ordered the work as Browse and Book -> Real Provider Self-Service -> Authentication and Ownership -> Booking Integrity -> Payment Boundary, with dependencies called out per slice.

dimension_scores.observation: The first slice targets the highest-value learning by validating the core booking flow before mixing in integration-heavy features like payments.
dimension_scores.evidence: They chose "demand side first" and "ultra_thin" specifically to validate the booking experience without auth, payments, search, or provider tooling.

dimension_scores.observation: The slice definitions are specific enough that another developer could begin implementation with minimal clarification.
dimension_scores.evidence: Each slice includes scope, anti-scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and complexity in artifacts/slices-module-04.md.

dimension_scores.observation: When stakeholder pressure arrived, the student responded quickly with a coherent option that preserved learning value while still addressing the investor concern.
dimension_scores.evidence: They proposed "a separate Slice 1.5 payment spike instead of expanding Slice 1" and stated that fully integrated payments by Friday would require explicit cuts elsewhere.

dimension_scores.observation: Taken together, the slices assemble into a coherent product path from seeded booking proof to integrity and payment boundary work.
dimension_scores.evidence: They kept the first slice end-to-end testable and later introduced booking integrity and payment boundary slices rather than leaving gaps between flows.

strengths: Strong scope discipline: the anti-scope lists were detailed enough to protect the thin slice from accidental expansion.
Strong stakeholder adaptation: they turned a risky last-minute payment request into a separate proof slice instead of destabilizing the core demo plan.
data.recommendation: In Module 05, convert the first two slices into task tickets with the same precision you used here for scope and anti-scope so an AI agent could execute them without guessing.
